body-large.purpose: Primary instructional and supporting text; all other roles inherit the Material 3 type scale.

shadows.name: stage-float
shadows.purpose: The reader dock, which hovers free of every screen edge over arbitrary artwork.

shadows.name: stage-panel
shadows.purpose: Reader panels that slide over the page.

shadows.name: material-overlay-only
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, sheets, and menus; resting content in the Study and Workbench stays tonal and flat.

motion.name: state-feedback
motion.purpose: Selection, control visibility, and ordinary state transitions.

motion.name: directional-navigation
motion.purpose: Preserve spatial direction when entering and leaving reading surfaces.

motion.name: tab-crossfade
motion.purpose: Top-level tab switches, kept distinct from the outer push transition.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Fallback when system animations are disabled or reduced.

breakpoints.name: expanded
breakpoints.value: tablet width; navigation rail or drawer

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Single clear recovery or permission action, styled from Material roles.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 48px; padding: 0 24px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: #2B2B2E; color: #FFFFFF; font: 500 14px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; transition: filter 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.12); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1685A9; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(.98); }

components.name: Outlined Field
components.description: Outlined text input for exact values such as hexadecimal colors and numeric limits.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 4px; color: #444448; font: 500 12px/16px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field input { min-height: 48px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid #7E7E84; border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: #2B2B2E; font: 400 16px/24px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field input:hover { border-color: #444448; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { border: 2px solid #2B2B2E; outline: none; }

components.name: Bottom Navigation Item
components.description: Compact phone navigation with a quiet pill-shaped selected state.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { min-width: 72px; height: 48px; padding: 4px 8px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: #606065; font: 500 12px/16px system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-nav-icon { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 56px; height: 32px; margin: 0 auto; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-nav-item-selected { color: #2B2B2E; } .ds-nav-item-selected .ds-nav-icon { background: #C7C7CC; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1685A9; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Comic Card
components.description: Image-led, flat comic entry with restrained metadata. Identical for local files and comic sources; only density differs per surface.
components.css: .ds-comic-card { width: 152px; color: #2B2B2E; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-comic-cover { aspect-ratio: 2 / 3; border-radius: 8px; background: #C7C7CC; } .ds-comic-card strong { display: block; margin-top: 4px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; } .ds-comic-card small { color: #606065; font-size: 12px; line-height: 16px; } .ds-comic-card:focus-within .ds-comic-cover { outline: 3px solid #1685A9; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Reader Dock
components.description: The floating reading dock: one near-opaque black surface that hovers over the page and collects every reading tool.
components.css: .ds-stage { display: grid; place-items: end stretch; width: 320px; height: 180px; padding: 4px 16px 12px; background: #000000; } .ds-reader-dock { display: flex; align-items: center; height: 60px; padding: 4px 6px; border-radius: 28px; background: rgba(0,0,0,.95); box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.55); } .ds-dock-item { flex: 1; height: 48px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: transparent; color: rgba(255,255,255,.7); font: 500 12px/16px system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); } .ds-dock-item-active { background: rgba(22,133,169,.28); color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-dock-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FFFFFF; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Reader Overlay
components.description: Compact transient status surface over the black reading stage.
components.css: .ds-reader-stage { display: grid; place-items: end center; width: 240px; height: 160px; padding: 16px; background: #000000; } .ds-reader-overlay { padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 12px; background: rgba(0,0,0,.5); color: #FFFFFF; font: 500 12px/16px system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Selected Reader Thumbnail
components.description: Directional page thumbnail with a restrained accent selection state.
components.css: .ds-reader-thumb { width: 56px; height: 80px; border: 1px solid #1685A9; border-radius: 4px; background: #303030; transform: scale(1.15); transform-origin: bottom center; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); } .ds-reader-thumb:hover { filter: brightness(1.15); } .ds-reader-thumb:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #FFFFFF; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-reader-thumb:active { transform: scale(1.1); }

components.name: OCR Region Mark
components.description: A mark drawn on artwork rather than chrome on black: fixed high-contrast signal colors, visible only while OCR selection is active.
components.css: .ds-ocr-canvas { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 240px; height: 140px; background: #494949; } .ds-ocr-region { padding: 6px 12px; border: 1.8px solid #00E5FF; border-radius: 4px; background: rgba(0,229,255,.38); box-shadow: 0 0 18px rgba(0,176,255,.26), inset 0 0 0 1.2px rgba(255,255,255,.88); color: #FFFFFF; font: 500 14px/20px system-ui, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview: Inkleaf should feel like ink moving only when the reader asks it to move. The interface is quiet at rest, then becomes expressive through page changes, gestures, selection feedback, and transitions that preserve spatial continuity. Material 3 Expressive supplies the shape and motion vocabulary, but the comic remains visually dominant. Every screen belongs to exactly one of three surfaces, and the surface decides the rules: the Stage is the comic itself and anything drawn over it, pure black and unthemed; the Study is where the user browses and chooses, fully themed, flat, image-led, and shared by local files and online sources alike; the Workbench is where the user configures, denser and more verbose but still flat and themed. The prose of this system is direction and deliberately carries no measurements: exact values live in the token block and in the code, because sizes will keep changing while the direction should not. Colors are the exception, because the seeds are identity rather than implementation.
keyCharacteristics: Dynamic Material color derived from a user-selected seed or Android wallpaper.
Tonal, flat-at-rest surfaces with elevation reserved for things that truly float.
A compact, consistent spacing rhythm that stays tight through content areas.
Familiar Material controls with restrained Expressive shape and motion.
One reading Stage, black and unthemed, shared by local files and online sources alike.

rules.name: The Seed, Not Swatches Rule
rules.body: Store and expose color seeds; generate the complete Material role scheme at runtime through Material Kolor or Android Dynamic Color.

rules.name: The Neutral Ink Rule
rules.body: Soft Charcoal Ink always uses the Neutral palette style. Never allow a chromatic generator to turn it into purple-gray.

rules.name: The Comic Owns the Stage Rule
rules.body: On the Stage, the page dominates. Theme color appears only as a controlled accent for selection, progress, and actionable state.

rules.name: The Chrome and the Mark Rule
rules.body: Stage chrome sits on known black, so it may use the theme accent with a luminance guard. A mark drawn on top of the artwork sits on unknown imagery, where no theme-derived color can be trusted to stay legible, so it uses a fixed high-contrast signal instead. Signal colors are permitted only for marks on artwork, only while their tool is active, and never as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Material Role Rule
rules.body: Choose typography by semantic Material role. Never hand-pick an isolated text size to make one screen feel more dramatic.

rules.name: The Comic Is the Display Face Rule
rules.body: App typography must not compete with cover art or page imagery. No decorative display fonts in navigation, buttons, labels, or reader controls.

rules.name: The Metadata Stays Small Rule
rules.body: Everything a source supplies about a comic — author, update time, tags, chapter counts, availability — is label-weight supporting text. A title is a title whether it came from a file name or from a plugin; metadata never grows to compete with it.

rules.name: The Tonal First Rule
rules.body: Use Material surface roles before adding shadow. If a resting card needs a wide decorative shadow to read as a card, the hierarchy is wrong.

rules.name: The Overlay Earns Elevation Rule
rules.body: Only an element that interrupts or overlays the current plane may use visible elevation.

rules.name: The Outline Groups, The Shadow Floats Rule
rules.body: In the Workbench, related settings are grouped with an outline, a tonal container, or a divider — never by lifting a resting card off the page. Shadow means 'this is above the plane you were on', and a settings group is not.

dos: Do name a screen's surface — Stage, Study, or Workbench — before deciding how it should look.
Do keep the comic visually dominant and reveal controls in response to reader intent.
Do use MaterialTheme.colorScheme roles for Study and Workbench surfaces, generated from the selected seed or Android wallpaper.
Do give local and online comics the same entry vocabulary, and let density differ per surface because the task differs.
Do build spacing from the one shared scale, staying in its tighter steps for most content.
Do use standard Material 3 Expressive components and state behavior before creating custom controls.
Do preserve the platform's minimum touch target even when the visible icon or swatch is smaller.
Do use motion to explain page direction, selection, entry, exit, and transient control state.
Do show source, plugin, and cache state as plain text where the user is already looking.
donts: Don't build recommendation surfaces Inkleaf invents for itself: house-curated rankings, editorial slots, promotional banners, achievement badges, or any entry point that competes with the user's own comics for attention. Presenting a source's declared content flows is legitimate; dressing them up as Inkleaf's own merchandising is not.
Don't create feature-heavy, visually noisy interfaces, and don't let secondary tools distract from choosing a comic and reading it.
Don't style an online comic differently from a local one. Availability may show; origin may not.
Don't interrupt reading for a failure that can be recovered or degraded silently.
Don't use Expressive motion, shape, or color as ambient decoration; every expressive choice must communicate state or movement.
Don't hard-code app surface colors when a Material color role exists, and don't use a signal color anywhere except as a mark on artwork.
Don't add decorative shadows to resting cards or pair a thin border with a wide soft shadow.
Don't add nested cards, oversized corner radii, gradient text, glassmorphism, decorative grids, or striped backgrounds.
Don't port iOS navigation, dialogs, switches, or back behavior into the Android interface.
